terrace_collapse_watch.name: Terrace Collapse Watch
terrace_collapse_watch.observation: Where no one mends the terrace walls, the first hard rain carries a hillside of soil into the gully below.

runoff_catchment_fields.name: Runoff Catchment Fields
runoff_catchment_fields.observation: Low stone walls on the bare hillsides lead the rare rain down onto walled fields in the valley floor.

failed_drain_marsh_return.name: Returning Fever Marsh
failed_drain_marsh_return.observation: When the ditches silt and the drains fail, the marsh creeps back over the fields, and with it the autumn fevers.

abandoned_land_regrowth.name: Regrowth on Abandoned Fields
abandoned_land_regrowth.observation: Fields left empty grow up in thorn and birch, and the village claims the new wood and grazing.

wildlife_return_watch.name: Returning Wild Beasts
wildlife_return_watch.observation: Deer, boar and wolf come back into the districts people have left, and the hunters mark their return.

valley_sediment_burial.name: Buried Valley Floors
valley_sediment_burial.observation: Diggers find old walls buried under a man's height of silt washed down from the cleared hills above.

dim_sun_years.name: Dim-Sun Years
dim_sun_years.observation: The old people tell of years when the sun shone weak and the harvest failed, and the granaries are filled against their return.

well_spacing_rules.name: Well Spacing Rules
well_spacing_rules.observation: No new well may be dug within a set distance of a neighbour's, lest both run dry.

licensed_estuary_weirs.name: Licensed Estuary Weirs
licensed_estuary_weirs.observation: Each stretch of the estuary has its one licensed weir, and no more may be built.

fen_commons.name: Fen Commons
fen_commons.observation: The fen is shared out by custom: reed for thatch, fowl and eels for the pot, and turf for the fire.

mast_count_pannage.name: Mast-Counted Pannage
mast_count_pannage.observation: Each autumn the wardens judge the acorn and beech mast and set how many swine may run in the wood.

endowed_reclamation.name: Endowed Reclamation
endowed_reclamation.observation: A community living under a rule clears scrub and marsh through generations of patient labor and turns it to field and orchard.
endowed_reclamation.ability_reason: Waste ground that no single family could afford to clear becomes farmland, because the community never dies and never tires.
endowed_reclamation.social_consequence: The communities grow rich in land, and the commoners who grazed the waste lose it.

seabird_colony_shares.name: Seabird Colony Shares
seabird_colony_shares.observation: Each household takes its fixed share of eggs and young birds from the cliffs, and the colony returns every spring.

village_wood_reeves.name: Village Wood-Reeves
village_wood_reeves.observation: The village wood-reeve marks which trees may be felled and doles out firewood by the household.

summer_shielings.name: Summer Shielings
summer_shielings.observation: In summer the herds go up to the high pastures with the dairy workers, and the valley meadows are left to grow hay.

fixed_charcoal_hearths.name: Fixed Charcoal Hearths
fixed_charcoal_hearths.observation: Colliers burn charcoal on the same levelled hearths inside the coppice each round, instead of clearing fresh ground.

quickset_hedges.name: Quickset Hedges
quickset_hedges.observation: Thorn cuttings planted along a bank grow into a living hedge that no cow can push through.

managed_heathland.name: Managed Heathland
managed_heathland.observation: The heath is burned in patches, cut for turf and grazed, so it stays open ground instead of turning to scrub.

reserved_hunting_rights.name: Reserved Hunting Rights
reserved_hunting_rights.observation: Game belongs to the lord, and a commoner caught with a deer is fined or loses his holding.
reserved_hunting_rights.social_consequence: Poaching becomes the commoners' quiet war against the lords.

wolf_bounties.name: Wolf Bounties
wolf_bounties.observation: The district pays a set price for every wolf's head brought in, and paid hunters range the hills.

locust_bounty_campaigns.name: Locust Bounty Campaigns
locust_bounty_campaigns.observation: Officials march the villagers out to dig locust eggs and pay grain for every basket of hoppers caught.

fur_beast_depletion.name: Trapped-Out Rivers
fur_beast_depletion.observation: Beaver and otter are gone from the settled rivers, and the trappers must go far into the wild country for pelts.

turf_manuring_depletion.name: Stripped Heaths
turf_manuring_depletion.observation: Years of cutting heath turf to spread with dung on the fields leave the heath bare sand, and the elders see it.

mill_dam_height_limits.name: Mill-Dam Height Limits
mill_dam_height_limits.observation: A mark cut in the bank fixes how high the miller may raise his dam, so the meadows upstream do not drown.

irrigation_water_tribunals.name: Irrigation Water Tribunals
irrigation_water_tribunals.observation: Each week the water judges sit at the canal gate and settle, before everyone, whose turn it is to open his sluice.
irrigation_water_tribunals.ability_reason: Quarrels over water are settled every week before they turn to feuds, so one irrigated valley can be shared by thousands.

introduced_weed_watch.name: Introduced Weed Watch
introduced_weed_watch.observation: New crops from far lands bring strange weeds and pests, and villagers learn their look and pull them before they spread.

storm_surge_records.name: Storm-Surge Records
storm_surge_records.observation: The height of each great sea flood is cut into a stone at the harbor, and the dikes are raised above the mark.

drifting_sand_burial.name: Drifting Sand
drifting_sand_burial.observation: Sand blown off the overgrazed heath buries fields and houses, and the herders are ordered to thin their flocks.
drifting_sand_burial.social_consequence: Herders forced to sell half their flocks blame the farmers who complained.

common_fallow_grazing_rule.name: Common Fallow Grazing
common_fallow_grazing_rule.observation: After harvest the whole village's beasts graze the fallow field together, and their dung feeds next year's crop.

licensed_forest_clearing.name: Licensed Forest Clearing
licensed_forest_clearing.observation: No one may clear the forest edge for new fields without a licence and a fee.
licensed_forest_clearing.ability_reason: The realm decides how much forest to give up for fields, instead of losing it one clearing at a time.
licensed_forest_clearing.social_consequence: Land-hungry younger sons pay for licences they can ill afford, or clear by stealth.

peat_fuel_cutting.name: Peat Fuel Cutting
peat_fuel_cutting.observation: In the treeless lowlands, turves of peat are cut, stacked and dried to burn in place of wood.
peat_fuel_cutting.social_consequence: The old cuttings fill with water and become lakes where fields once stood.

protected_hawk_eyries.name: Protected Hawk Eyries
protected_hawk_eyries.observation: The eyries of hunting hawks are guarded, and taking a young falcon without leave is a crime.

windy_hill_smelting_hearths.name: Windy-Hill Smelting Hearths
windy_hill_smelting_hearths.observation: Lead is smelted on windy hilltops, where the wind drives the hearth fumes away from farms and wells.

oak_bark_seasons.name: Oak Bark Seasons
oak_bark_seasons.observation: Oak bark is stripped only in spring, when it peels clean, and the coppiced stools sprout again.

sluiced_polders.name: Sluiced Polders
sluiced_polders.observation: Dikes ring the salt marsh, and sluices open at low tide to let the water out, until the marsh becomes meadow.
sluiced_polders.ability_reason: Land won from the sea feeds a growing people without a single tree felled.
sluiced_polders.social_consequence: The dike levy falls on every holding, and the fowlers lose their marsh.

marked_tree_sales.name: Marked-Tree Sales
marked_tree_sales.observation: The forester blazes each tree that may be sold with his axe mark, and no other may be felled.

forest_perambulation.name: Walking the Forest Bounds
forest_perambulation.observation: Once in a generation the old men and the boys walk the forest bounds together, so the marks are remembered.

forest_law_courts.name: Forest Law Courts
forest_law_courts.observation: The ruler's forests have their own law, their own courts and their own wardens, and whole districts live under them.
forest_law_courts.ability_reason: Great tracts of woodland are held back from the plough and the axe by a law with its own judges.
forest_law_courts.social_consequence: Villages inside the forest bounds may not clear, hunt or fence, and they hate the wardens.

woodbank_enclosures.name: Woodbank Enclosures
woodbank_enclosures.observation: A bank and ditch around each cut coppice keep the cattle from browsing the new shoots.

river_fishery_wardens.name: River Fishery Wardens
river_fishery_wardens.observation: Wardens patrol the river in the spawning season and cut any net with too fine a mesh.

paled_deer_parks.name: Paled Deer Parks
paled_deer_parks.observation: A park fenced with oak pales holds the lord's deer and keeps them off the peasants' corn.

salt_pan_fuel_draw.name: Salt-Pan Fuel Draw
salt_pan_fuel_draw.observation: The salt boilers burn a whole wood each season to feed their pans, and the coast around them lies bare.
salt_pan_fuel_draw.social_consequence: Salt grows cheap while firewood grows dear.

woodland_common_allowances.name: Common-Wood Allowances
woodland_common_allowances.observation: Each holding has its allowance: so much firewood, so many poles for fencing, pannage for so many swine.

coppice_with_standards.name: Coppice with Standards
coppice_with_standards.observation: The underwood is cut every dozen years for poles and fuel, while chosen oaks grow on above it for beams.
coppice_with_standards.ability_reason: One wood now yields firewood every generation and great beams every century, without ever being cleared.

relict_wild_cattle_reserves.name: Last Wild Cattle
relict_wild_cattle_reserves.observation: The great wild oxen now live only in one guarded forest, and killing one is forbidden.

mine_water_complaints.name: Mine-Water Complaints
mine_water_complaints.observation: Farmers downstream of the mines bring their poisoned meadows to court, and the miners are ordered to settle their water.

kiln_fuel_licences.name: Kiln Fuel Licences
kiln_fuel_licences.observation: Lime and brick burners need a licence to take fuel, and each may take only so many loads a year.

downstream_trade_quarters.name: Downstream Trade Quarters
downstream_trade_quarters.observation: Tanners and dyers must work below the town, where their foul water no longer runs past the wells.

sea_coal_substitution.name: Sea-Coal Burning
sea_coal_substitution.observation: Where firewood runs short, coal washed up on the shore or dug from shallow pits is burned in its place.
sea_coal_substitution.social_consequence: Coal smoke hangs sour over the towns that burn it.

warren_escape_liability.name: Warren Liability
warren_escape_liability.observation: When rabbits escape the lord's warren and eat a neighbour's corn, the warrener must pay for the damage.

stinted_commons.name: Stinted Commons
stinted_commons.observation: Each holding may graze only so many beasts on the common, and the manor jury fines any who put on more.
stinted_commons.ability_reason: Shared pasture is no longer grazed to bare earth, because each household's share is counted and enforced.
stinted_commons.social_consequence: Cottagers with no land lose the few beasts they grazed by custom.

crop_limit_shift_watch.name: Shifting Crop Limits
crop_limit_shift_watch.observation: Old men remember vines ripening on hills where the grapes now fail, and farmers change what they sow.

dike_boards.name: Dike Boards
dike_boards.observation: Everyone behind the dike pays the dike levy and elects the reeves who inspect and repair it.
dike_boards.ability_reason: A whole low country keeps its dikes whole, because the work and the cost are shared by all who live behind them.

wool_flock_overgrazing.name: Overgrazed Uplands
wool_flock_overgrazing.observation: The great sheep flocks strip the uplands bare, and the stewards cut the flocks back.

bird_observation_treatise.name: Treatise on Birds
bird_observation_treatise.observation: A falconer's book describes birds from long watching: how they fly, feed, nest and moult.

shellfish_closed_seasons.name: Shellfish Closed Seasons
shellfish_closed_seasons.observation: Oyster and mussel beds are closed in the summer months, when they breed and when they sicken those who eat them.

ironmaster_coppice_contracts.name: Ironmaster Coppice Contracts
ironmaster_coppice_contracts.observation: The ironmaster buys a whole wood and cuts it in rotation, so his hearths never run out of charcoal.

itinerant_forest_glassworks.name: Wandering Forest Glassworks
itinerant_forest_glassworks.observation: The glassmakers build their furnace in a wood, burn the wood to ash for their glass, and move on to the next.
itinerant_forest_glassworks.social_consequence: Villagers who wake to find their wood sold to the glassmakers have no firewood that winter.

steward_husbandry_treatises.name: Husbandry Treatises
steward_husbandry_treatises.observation: Estate stewards write down what they have learned of marling, stocking and yields, for those who come after.

drained_land_subsidence.name: Sinking Drained Land
drained_land_subsidence.observation: The drained peat shrinks and sinks until the fields lie below the river, and the wise foresee that the water must one day be lifted out.

nitre_earth_leaching.name: Nitre-Earth Leaching
nitre_earth_leaching.observation: Earth from stable floors and old middens is soaked in tubs, and the liquor is boiled down for its nitre.

river_offal_bans.name: River Offal Bans
river_offal_bans.observation: The town forbids butchers and householders to throw offal and dung in the river, on pain of a fine.
river_offal_bans.ability_reason: The town's river becomes fit to draw from again, and the summer sickness that followed the butchers eases.

coal_smoke_limits.name: Coal-Smoke Limits
coal_smoke_limits.observation: The burning of sea-coal is forbidden in the town while the council sits, and the lime-burners must go back to wood.
coal_smoke_limits.ability_reason: A town can now choose how much smoke it will breathe, trading cheap fuel for cleaner air.

weir_fish_gaps.name: Weir Fish Gaps
weir_fish_gaps.observation: Every weir and mill dam must leave a gap open, so the salmon can pass upstream to spawn.

felling_rotation_ordinance.name: Felling Rotation Ordinance
felling_rotation_ordinance.observation: The forest ordinance fixes the age at which each kind of wood may be cut, and the order of felling.

nitrate_cultivation.observation: Heaped beds of dung, lime and earth are kept moist and turned for years, and the nitre that blooms in them is scraped and leached.
nitrate_cultivation.ability_reason: Nitre no longer depends on scraping old stables: it can be grown in beds, in quantity, year after year.

marginal_land_retreat.name: Retreat from Marginal Land
marginal_land_retreat.observation: After the wet summers and the famines, the poorest hill farms are given up and the heather creeps back.
marginal_land_retreat.social_consequence: Families driven off the hills crowd into the valley villages.

glacier_advance_records.name: Glacier Advance Records
glacier_advance_records.observation: The herdsmen record the year the ice came down over the high pasture where their grandfathers grazed.

avalanche_guard_forests.name: Avalanche-Guard Forests
avalanche_guard_forests.observation: The forest above the village is closed to the axe, for its trees hold back the winter snowslides.

drowned_land_abandonment.name: Drowned Land Given Back
drowned_land_abandonment.observation: Where the sea breaks the dike once too often, the land is given back to salt marsh and a new dike is built further inland.

daily_weather_diaries.name: Daily Weather Diaries
daily_weather_diaries.observation: A scholar notes the wind, the rain and the warmth of every day, year after year, in a long ledger.

conifer_seed_sowing.name: Conifer Seed Sowing
conifer_seed_sowing.observation: Fir and pine seed is gathered and sown on cut-over ground, and within a lifetime there is forest again.
